metadata.title: As AI hardware sells off, is this chip designer now deeply undervalued?

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — The recent pullback across artificial intelligence hardware has battered semiconductor leaders indiscriminately, pulling down stocks regardless of their underlying margins or business models. Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) has tumbled 18.8% over the past month to $293.69, caught in the same aggressive tech rotation that pressured Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA).
Yet the sell-off prices Broadcom like a commoditized hardware supplier, completely overlooking its structural competitive advantages. In addition to high-margin recurring revenue from its VMware infrastructure software suite, Broadcom holds an estimated 70% market share in custom AI silicon accelerators (XPUs) co-designed with hyperscalers like Alphabet and Meta Platforms—a lucrative market where competitors like Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) are racing to catch up.
Spotting when a broad market pullback indiscriminately punishes high-margin technology leaders is what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models are designed to identify. Rather than chasing crowded trades, the Tech Titans strategy focuses on capital-efficient cash generators, with an active November portfolio holding an enterprise collaboration software platform, an essential semiconductor inspection monopoly, and a mission-critical cloud delivery network.
The operating numbers tell a very different story. In fiscal third-quarter 2026, revenue rose 86% year-over-year to $29.6 billion, led by a 221% jump in AI semiconductor revenue to $16.7 billion, which now accounts for 56% of total revenue. Shipments of XPUs—the custom accelerators Broadcom builds for tier-one cloud hyperscalers—expanded more than 3.5-fold compared to the prior-year period.
According to data tracked inside the Broadcom Pro Research Report, the company controls roughly 70% of the custom AI chip market and approximately 90% of data center switching silicon. Six major XPU customers, including Alphabet, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta, are committed to multi-year development roadmaps, creating exceptionally high customer switching costs. Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $34.8 billion, including $21.7 billion from AI silicon, and outlined ambitious long-term AI semiconductor targets of $115 billion for fiscal 2027 and $230 billion for fiscal 2028.
Software integration further reinforces cash flow. Infrastructure software revenue expanded 29% year-over-year to $8.8 billion in the quarter at an exceptional 84% operating margin, lifting total consolidated operating margin to 67.9%. Free cash flow reached an all-time record of $13.7 billion, representing a remarkable 46% of revenue.
A valuation disconnect in high-margin tech
Against that operational backdrop, current valuation multiples appear compressed. The stock trades at 36.6 times trailing earnings and 24.4 times forward estimates, yielding an unusually low PEG ratio of 0.37. Based on consensus Wall Street estimates projecting fiscal 2028 earnings of $32.50 per share, the multiple drops to roughly 9 times.
InvestingPro's Fair Value suite—which aggregates multiple independent discounted cash flow and relative valuation models—benchmarks Broadcom at $403.06 per share, indicating 37.2% upside from current levels alongside an official "Undervalued" label. InvestingPro's Financial Health framework rates the company "Great," supported by strong balance sheet liquidity and $5.6 billion in long-term debt repayments completed in the third quarter alone.
Wall Street analysts maintain an even more bullish outlook. The consensus price target sits at $533.42, pointing to roughly 82% upside, with the street-low target anchored at $400. While potential risks include a contingent liability of up to $43 billion tied to AI rack customer financing, gross margins guided toward 73%, and 22 downward analyst revisions over the past 90 days, the underlying cash flow provides a substantial margin of safety.
Investors can review full XPU production schedules, VMware subscription transition metrics, and cash flow durability inside the Broadcom Pro Research Report.
Broadcom's recent operating results illustrate the disconnect between short-term market sentiment and long-term earnings power. Operating with an elite 67.9% operating margin and generating a record $13.7 billion in quarterly free cash flow, the business delivers cash conversion that speculative hardware suppliers cannot match.
Recognizing when broad sector volatility obscures underlying balance sheet strength is why ProPicks AI evaluates fundamentals every month. The Tech Titans strategy systematically reallocates capital into high-conviction operators that turn data center spending into organic free cash flow without taking on excessive leverage—spanning developer software platforms, chip inspection monopolies, and enterprise cloud infrastructure.
